title: CORS Wildcard + Credentials on All Routes Enables Cross-Origin Credential Theft
description: All backend routes reflect arbitrary attacker-controlled Origin headers verbatim while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This includes the null origin, enabling sandboxed iframe attacks. An attacker can exfiltrate authenticated user JWTs/sessions from any domain.
evidence_safe: OPTIONS /health with Origin: http://evil.com returned access-control-allow-origin: http://evil.com and access-control-allow-credentials: true. Tested on all routes.

title: CORS null Origin Reflection with Credentials Enables Sandboxed Iframe Attack
description: The backend reflects the literal 'null' Origin header with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Browsers send Origin: null from sandboxed iframes (sandbox attribute without allow-same-origin), enabling an attacker to bypass SameSite cookie restrictions via a sandboxed iframe hosted anywhere.
evidence_safe: Origin: null returned access-control-allow-origin: null and access-control-allow-credentials: true, enabling sandboxed iframe exploitation.

title: Auth-Gated SSRF Candidate Endpoints Present (/proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render)
description: Multiple endpoints that commonly perform server-side URL fetching exist on the backend (/proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import). All return 401 unauthenticated. If authentication is obtained via CORS exploitation, these endpoints are high-probability SSRF vectors to reach Azure IMDS at 169.254.169.254 and obtain managed identity credentials.
evidence_safe: Endpoints /proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render, /preview, /import exist (401 auth-gated). POST /fetch accepts JSON body. These are likely SSRF vectors post-authentication.

title: Technology Stack Disclosure via X-Powered-By: Express Header
description: All responses include X-Powered-By: Express header, confirming Node.js/Express backend. Error pages additionally leak Express internal routing format (e.g., 'Cannot DELETE /health'). This enables targeted selection of framework-specific exploits including prototype pollution and Express-specific request handling quirks.
evidence_safe: HTTP response header x-powered-by: Express present on all responses. Error pages show 'Cannot DELETE /health' format confirming Express routing.

title: Environment Name Disclosed in Unauthenticated /health Endpoint
description: The publicly accessible /health endpoint returns {"status":"ok","env":"production"}, confirming the deployment environment is production. This reduces attacker uncertainty when targeting the highest-privilege environment and confirms live production systems are in scope.
evidence_safe: GET /health returns {"status":"ok","env":"production"} without authentication. Confirms production deployment.

title: Azure Container App Internal Backend URL Exposed in Client-Side JavaScript Bundle
description: The NextAuth.js bundle served at revops-dev.vercel.app contains a hardcoded reference to the internal backend API URL: https://revops-dev.livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io. This URL is publicly accessible, responds to unauthenticated requests on /health, and exposes the internal infrastructure topology. Direct probing of the backend API is possible without going through the frontend.
evidence_safe: String 'revops-dev.livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io' found in NextAuth bundle chunk e31b6e95b36824c0.js; /health returns HTTP 200 with Express server
evidence_quarantined: URL: https://revops-dev.livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io — found inline in JS bundle; /health returns {"status":"ok","env":"production"}

title: Git Commit SHA Hardcoded in Vercel Production Bundle (Source Version Fingerprinting)
description: The Datadog RUM initialization bundle contains the literal git commit SHA 61c5fdeac36ed85a883ae93b78c06d03f9f4e4a1 baked in as the application version string. This confirms the exact source code version deployed to production and can aid an attacker in identifying known vulnerabilities associated with that code version or correlating it with any future source code disclosure.
evidence_safe: Git SHA 61c5fdeac36ed85a883ae93b78c06d03f9f4e4a1 found as hardcoded version string in Datadog RUM init block in public Vercel JS bundle
evidence_quarantined: Datadog RUM init: version:"1.0.0" with SHA 61c5fdeac36ed85a883ae93b78c06d03f9f4e4a1 baked in; confirms production bundle identity

title: Internal Contributor Email Addresses Exposed in Public GitHub Repository Git History
description: The public CoPoint-Data/BMAD-METHOD GitHub repository exposes internal contributor email addresses in commit history, including dave.sims@hey.com (primary CoPoint maintainer) and brianmadison@Brians-MacBook-Pro.local (containing the local machine hostname). These can be used for spear-phishing, credential stuffing, or social engineering attacks against CoPoint AI staff.
evidence_safe: Git log reveals contributor emails: dave.sims@hey.com (CoPoint maintainer), brianmadison@Brians-MacBook-Pro.local in public BMAD-METHOD repo

title: Internal Application Name and Datadog RUM Configuration Exposed in Client Bundle
description: The Vercel production bundle exposes internal application metadata: the service is named 'revops-crm', environment is 'production', and uses Datadog RUM on datadoghq.com. The NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_APPLICATION_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_CLIENT_TOKEN environment variable names are referenced, confirming Datadog is instrumented. Datadog client tokens, if obtained, would allow reading RUM session data.
evidence_safe: JS bundle exposes: service name 'revops-crm', env 'production', Datadog RUM on datadoghq.com; env var names NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_APPLICATION_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_CLIENT_TOKEN referenced

title: Active subdomains enumerated via certificate transparency: revops, www, accelerate, pay
description: crt.sh and subfinder revealed 5 subdomains: revops.copointdata.com (production CRM, live), www.copointdata.com (live), accelerate.copointdata.com (cert exists, NXDOMAIN), pay.copointdata.com (cert exists, NXDOMAIN), www.pay.copointdata.com. The dormant subdomains with valid certs and no DNS records may represent future attack surface.
evidence_safe: crt.sh JSON response listing copointdata.com subdomains: revops, www, accelerate, pay, www.pay — all confirmed via DNS resolution

title: DMARC policy=none enables email spoofing for @copointdata.com
description: The DMARC record for copointdata.com is set to p=none, meaning no enforcement action is taken on emails that fail DMARC checks. Combined with the absence of DKIM records, an attacker could potentially craft spoofed emails appearing to originate from @copointdata.com addresses, facilitating phishing attacks against employees or customers.
evidence_safe: DNS TXT _dmarc.copointdata.com returned: v=DMARC1;p=none; — monitoring only, no enforcement

title: Developer identity confirmed: David Sims (dave.sims@hey.com, github.com/dave-sims)
description: GitHub profile dave-sims identified as David Sims, the developer contact for CoPoint AI (dave.sims@hey.com). Profile has 6 public repos demonstrating Go, Python, and React Native skills. No copointdata.com email exposed publicly. External email uses Hey.com (Basecamp) service.
evidence_safe: GitHub API: login=dave-sims, name=David Sims, public_repos=6. External contact email dave.sims@hey.com from GitHub commit data.

title: Azure AD tenant ID exposed in public NextAuth providers endpoint
description: The /api/auth/providers endpoint on revops.copointdata.com returns the Azure AD OAuth configuration including the tenant ID (9046c3d1-04fe-4afe-9e4f-9217f27b5a66) and callback URLs without authentication. This exposes the exact Azure tenant, enabling targeted reconnaissance of the Microsoft 365 environment.
evidence_safe: GET /api/auth/providers returned: azure-ad provider with signinUrl containing tenant ID 9046c3d1-04fe-4afe-9e4f-9217f27b5a66

title: Development environment revops-dev.vercel.app publicly accessible with same Azure AD auth
description: The development deployment at revops-dev.vercel.app is publicly reachable and uses the same Azure AD authentication configuration as production. The /api/auth/providers endpoint confirms Azure AD is the only auth provider. Dev environments often have relaxed security controls or debug features enabled.
evidence_safe: revops-dev.vercel.app returns HTTP 307 redirect to /login, /api/auth/providers returns azure-ad config. Dev environment publicly accessible.

title: Technology stack fingerprinted via client-side JS bundle: Next.js, Datadog, v0.dev, TanStack Query
description: The revops.copointdata.com login page exposes the full technology stack through its JavaScript bundle references and HTML meta tags: built with v0.dev (Vercel AI UI generator), Next.js with React Server Components, NextAuth.js, DatadogProvider (monitoring), PermissionsProvider, VersionProvider, and TanStack Query for state management. This aids targeted attack planning.
evidence_safe: HTML meta generator=v0.dev, JS bundle contains DatadogProvider, QueryProvider, PermissionsProvider, SessionProvider, VersionProvider component names

title: No DKIM records configured for copointdata.com — increases spoofing risk
description: DNS queries for selector1._domainkey.copointdata.com and selector2._domainkey.copointdata.com both return NXDOMAIN. Combined with DMARC p=none, the absence of DKIM means there is no cryptographic validation of outbound email, making spoofed emails from @copointdata.com indistinguishable from legitimate ones by receiving mail servers.
evidence_safe: DNS NXDOMAIN for selector1._domainkey.copointdata.com and selector2._domainkey.copointdata.com — no DKIM signing configured

title: Next.js 16.1.6 version disclosed in client-side JavaScript bundle
description: The production JavaScript bundle emits `window.next={version:"16.1.6",appDir:true}` and `window.next.turbopack=true`, exposing the exact Next.js version and build toolchain to unauthenticated clients. React version 19.3.0 is similarly disclosed in the framework chunk. This enables attackers to research version-specific future CVEs.
evidence_safe: window.next={version:"16.1.6",appDir:true} found in JS bundle chunk 7f9e9c54ac262de2.js; React 19.3.0 in 6fd9b82a5c9eca06.js

title: Express.js framework version disclosed via x-powered-by response header
description: The backend Azure Container Apps instance returns `x-powered-by: Express` on all HTTP responses including health and error endpoints. While the specific Express version is not disclosed, the framework fingerprint enables targeted exploitation research and is trivially suppressible.
evidence_safe: Response header x-powered-by: Express confirmed on Azure Container Apps backend; version number not disclosed but framework fingerprinted

title: CVE-2025-29927 Next.js middleware auth bypass: NOT VULNERABLE (version 16.1.6 >= 15.2.3)
description: CVE-2025-29927 affects Next.js < 15.2.3 and allows bypassing middleware authentication by sending a crafted x-middleware-subrequest header. Target is running Next.js 16.1.6 and is not affected. Active testing confirmed: bypass header returns identical 307 redirect to /login for all tested protected routes (/dashboard, /settings, /admin).
evidence_safe: Normal: HTTP 307 /dashboard->login. With x-middleware-subrequest bypass header: HTTP 307 (identical). Next.js 16.1.6 > 15.2.3 threshold. Not exploitable.

title: CVE-2023-48309 NextAuth.js open redirect: NOT EXPLOITABLE (callbackUrl validation active)
description: CVE-2023-48309 affects NextAuth.js < 4.24.5 and allows open redirect via callbackUrl parameter. Active testing confirmed NextAuth rejects external callbackUrls: POST to /api/auth/signin/azure-ad with callbackUrl=https://evil.attacker.com returns the internal signin URL, and the callback-url cookie is always set to the application origin. The cookie naming convention (__Host-next-auth.csrf-token) indicates v4.x.
evidence_safe: POST /api/auth/signin/azure-ad with callbackUrl=https://evil.attacker.com returned {url:https://revops-dev.vercel.app/api/auth/signin?csrf=true}. External URL rejected. Cookie callback-url always set to origin.
